chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated from al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hafs al-Jawhari, who said:

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) led us in the Maghrib prayer, and he prostrated the prostration of gratitude after the seventh [verse]. I said to him, 'Your fathers used to prostrate after the third.' He said, 'None of my fathers used to prostrate except after the seventh.'
And it has been narrated that the permissibility of prostration of gratitude after the Maghrib prayer is established.
ai.seo_question: Which verse of the Quran is associated with the prostration of gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr) according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam's precise adherence to the specific verse (Al-Isra, verse 109) for the prostration of gratitude, correcting the common assumption that his forefathers followed a different practice. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between established Sunnah and personal habit, while also affirming the permissibility of performing this voluntary prostration after the Maghrib prayer, often associated with the concept of *ta'tir* (dusting the forehead with earth).
